clue.text: Deity with nothing to work at is in complete armour

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
zero, the letter O
to ply a trade is to work at it

explanation.surface: A god with nothing to do is sitting in a full suit of armour.
explanation.walkthrough: PANOPLY first meant a knight's full suit of armour; 'is in' only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The original sense of the word is a full set of a soldier's protective gear.

clue.text: Capital people in pairs as they get sorted out

indicators.note: the letters of these words are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: City folk pair up and get organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of the French capital are the people of that city.

parts.note: pinchers are thieves or arresting police, both of whom are said to be busy grabbing

explanation.walkthrough: To pinch is slang both to steal and to arrest, so pinchers busy at it are grabbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Grabbing or arresting someone is slang for what pinchers do.

clue.text: All quiet among wild apes when sweeties appear

indicators.note: among says one word sits in the middle of the other
wild apes run riot, so their letters are scrambled

parts.note: still means silent and quiet

explanation.surface: Total silence falls among wild apes when sweets are handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' scrambles the apes, and 'All quiet' is a single synonym rather than two pieces; 'when ... appear' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Small flavoured lozenges are sweets, sweeties in British usage.

clue.text: But grief returns with the revolving (Shelley)

definitions.text: But grief returns with the revolving (Shelley)

parts.words: But grief returns with the revolving (Shelley)
parts.note: the line from Shelley's Adonais ends with the missing word

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: Shelley's Adonais has 'But grief returns with the revolving year'; the answer is the word that completes the line.
explanation.definitionFit: The cycle of the seasons that comes round again is the twelvemonth.

clue.text: Ritual is performed 'to a T for this bishop

indicators.note: a ritual that is performed is acted out, so its letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A ceremony is carried out perfectly for the benefit of a particular bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a T' looks like the idiom for 'perfectly', but it adds the letter T to RITUAL before the rearranging. A titular bishop holds the title of a see that no longer exists.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop named to an extinct see in name only is called a titular bishop.

clue.text: In the chess variety also knights test their strength

definitions.text: In the chess variety also knights test their strength

parts.words: In the chess variety also knights test their strength
parts.note: chess players meet in competition, and medieval knights jousted in a contest of the same name

explanation.walkthrough: Knights are chess pieces too, but here they are the jousting knights of the Middle Ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A competition, whether between chess players or jousting knights, is a series of contests.

parts.note: to stand someone a drink is to pay for it, so the invitation is to have one on you

explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing' is not 'permanent': to stand someone a drink is to pay for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something paid for on another's behalf is offered as a gift.

parts.note: blood-sucking worms that doctors used, and an old word for doctors themselves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Suckers' are not dupes but blood-sucking worms once applied by doctors.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood-sucking worms used in medicine, whose name was also old slang for physicians.

clue.text: Scolded the dog, although it was valued

definitions.meaning: to rate is an old verb for to scold or berate

explanation.walkthrough: 'although it was' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The old verb meaning to scold harshly shares its form with the word for assessed in worth.

clue.text: Take a sober turn 'in full dress

indicators.note: giving the word sober a turn twists its letters into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone sobers up while wearing formal clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonial gowns worn on formal occasions are the full dress of judges and dons.

clue.text: One of the Nine only meant, we hear, a bit of fun

parts.note: the Nine are the Muses of Greek myth, so one of them is a muse

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: the word meant, spoken, gives the syllable ending the answer

explanation.surface: One of the Muses only meant it as a bit of fun, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment or a diversion is a bit of fun.

definitions.meaning: strong liquor such as whisky or gin
a ghost or phantom, an old poetic sense

explanation.definitionFit: Spirits are strong alcohol, and a spirit is also a ghost, which poets call a shade.

parts.note: the gap is the missing word of the first line of Byron's Hebrew Melodies poem on a girl who died young

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: the line is 'Oh! snatched away in beauty's bloom', from Byron's Hebrew Melodies; the answer fills the dash.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in the quoted line means taken suddenly, as by an early death.

parts.note: written signs standing for ideas rather than sounds

explanation.definitionFit: Signs that stand directly for ideas, as in Chinese writing, are symbolic characters.

clue.text: Winged one in the wings on the-opening night doubtless !

definitions.text: Winged one in the wings on the-opening night doubtless !

parts.words: Winged one in the wings on the-opening night doubtless
parts.note: a heavenly being has wings, and a theatre's financial backer will be waiting in the wings on the first night

explanation.walkthrough: In theatre slang the backer who funds a show has a nickname taken from heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a winged heavenly messenger and a theatre's investor share this name.

clue.text: A Scotsman among godly believers having devilish inclinations

indicators.note: among says one word sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: deists believe in God but not revealed religion
mon is the Scots form of man

explanation.surface: A Scot among pious believers has a taste for the devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'godly believers' are deists, believers in a God known by reason alone; 'A' is a link word, since the Scots form needs no article.
explanation.definitionFit: Believers in or worshippers of evil spirits have leanings toward the diabolical.

clue.text: What a come-down at the day's end

definitions.text: What a come-down at the day's end

parts.words: What a come-down at the day's end
parts.note: darkness is said to fall each evening

explanation.walkthrough: 'come-down' looks like a disappointment; it is darkness that falls when the day ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is when night is said to fall at the close of day.

parts.note: units of grammar, and the punishments a judge hands down

explanation.definitionFit: Grammatical units and punishments imposed by a court share the same name.

parts.note: a doubter takes what he is told with a pinch of seasoning, served with a tiny spoon

explanation.walkthrough: A sceptic takes things 'with a pinch of salt'; the tiny spoon used at the table holds just such a pinch.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny spoon for the condiment cellar measures out the pinch a doubter needs.

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate commander in the American Civil War
a side is a group of supporters

explanation.surface: Southern supporters find somewhere to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'find' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheltered side, away from the wind, offers cover.

parts.note: the smallest unit of weight shares its name with a cereal crop

explanation.walkthrough: The smallest unit in the old British weight system is named after a single seed of wheat, which is also what a harvest brings in.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the tiniest unit of weight and the cereal crop gathered at harvest.

parts.note: a short song or melody, in the French form of the Italian diminutive

explanation.walkthrough: The Italian arietta is a short aria; give it a French ending and you have the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A short tune or song, spelt in the French manner.

parts.note: Hamlet's line to Horatio, here read as describing an excess

explanation.walkthrough: 'Something too much of this' is Hamlet's line to Horatio; read as words it describes an overabundance.
explanation.definitionFit: An excess or superabundance is literally too much of something.

clue.text: Go to Town, with the increase in price of ginger beer?

definitions.meaning: to make a quick visit to London

definitions.text: the increase in price of ginger beer
definitions.meaning: pop is fizzy drink, so pop going up is its price rising

explanation.walkthrough: 'Town' in British usage means London; 'with' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To nip up to the capital is one sense; fizzy drink rising in price is the other.

definitions.meaning: German white wines from the Rhine
the joints of an animal's hind leg

explanation.walkthrough: 'to go with' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhenish white wines are called by this name, and so are the hind-leg joints of a pig.

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
rife means widespread or abounding

explanation.surface: A street full of rows and arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter conflict and disputes amount to quarrelling.

parts.note: to let something go and a young sole share one word

explanation.walkthrough: A young sole is a small fish with the same name as letting something escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A small young sole, and the verb for letting something get away.

definitions.meaning: the head of a school or organisation
the capital sum of a loan or investment, on which interest is paid

explanation.definitionFit: The chief person is the head; the capital sum invested earns interest.

clue.text: Can't I have a caper for a change?

indicators.note: the letters of the words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they might have some fun for once.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotesque or playful leap is a caper.

clue.text: Last word about the let gives satisfaction

indicators.note: about means one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is the last word in a letter
a lease is the letting of a property

explanation.surface: Having the final say on the rental arrangement keeps everyone happy.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy someone is to give them pleasure.

parts.note: an artist's colour board sounds like a word for straw mattresses

explanation.walkthrough: Painters mix colours on a palette; straw mattresses are pallets, spelt differently but said the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw-filled mattresses share their sound with an artist's mixing board for colours.
